I feel like the newer star wars movies are missing a relatable human element. It's like everyone is operating on a binary switch for their emotions and there's no shades of anything. Characters don't seem to develop in any profound or unpredictable ways. One point in Rogue One's favor is that there aren't really any Jedi in it, which is rare for a Star Wars movie.

The Jedi are terrible characters because they're too much like morally superior supermen who can't lose a fight even against overwhelming odds. We've seen 20+ minutes of Jedi on storm trooper action too many times. It doesn't feel like an epic fight as much as it seems like a chore. The real cost of solar power is heavily disguised behind direct and indirect subsidies. Don't get me wrong, I can't wait for the day we shut down the last coal, oil, or natural gas power plant. I just don't think we're as close as the title implies.

In particular almost any new power plant would be less expensive than importing diesel to an island.

While solar is one of the biggest emerging energy fields it is still really underdeveloped in energy storage. For a real renewable solution we need battery or capacitance to store energy from peak sun and use it during peak usage.

For instance, early on winter morning there is a large demand for power when everyone starts waking up to get ready for the day. Coincidentally, there is almost zero sun out during this time. That means there MUST currently be some other form of more readily available energy available. Each type of generation has its own response time. Coal can take a couple hours to crank up before it hits peak, while natural gas can be ready to go in a matter of minutes. Nuclear on the other hand always offers the same generation but has waste products which there's currently no solution for.

So to me, it's not about eliminating these different types of energy, but advancing them to have less environmental impact and substituting renewables when it's reasonable to do so.

Battery technology is where you should look for the next huge breakthrough if solar is going to widespread adoption over other methods.

On a side note a really cool setup they have in South Carolina is a renewable dam energy. What they do is let water down the dam during the daytime when energy is expensive. At night they can pump water back up into the reservoir for cheaper than they can sell it for in the daytime. Sources like this are both renewable and offer massively on-demand energy - I wouldn't be surprised to see this start popping up more often.
